headline: Heterogeneity in susceptibility, environment and transmission shapes epidemic dynamics
label: Heterogeneity In Epidemic Population Dynamics
summary: Recent preprints encode stress, temperature-driven infection loss and individual transmission variance as explicit, analyzable model components.
synthesis: The dominant thread is heterogeneity introduced as an explicit model component whose functional form determines population-level behavior. The stress study contrasts deterministic and stochastic infection dynamics in a population where physiological stress alters disease susceptibility in aquatic environments. The Wolbachia study embeds temperature-driven infection loss in an impulsive ODE framework comparing wMelPop, wMel and wAlbB release strategies. The Moyal-Poisson mixture model links individual-based stochastic SIR transmission to macroscopic pandemic waves and recovers superspreading in SARS. The items differ in methods and maturity, so the shared element is methodological rather than a common result. What is new is the reduction of diverse sources, from susceptibility and environmental infection loss to individual transmission variance, into tractable model components.
